title: An infinite finitely presented residually finite 2-group
main_claim: Gamma = St_12(R), where R is the companion paper's finitely presented graded F_2-algebra with matrix-nil augmentation ideal, is residually finite via the degree truncations St_12(R/R_{>=d}). Hence G = ker(Gamma -> St_12(F_2)) is an infinite, finitely presented, residually finite group in which every element has 2-power order.
coverage:
I read every section of this paper except the detailed homological proof in the stability section; its conclusion (injectivity of St_12(R) -> St(R)) is also covered by the cited Suslin-Tulenbaev theorem, because R is local with stable rank 1. Checked line by line:
- Phase lemma: the backward induction for literal phases, the subword offset identity b+|p_v| = |p_w| + L_j a, the thresholds, and invariance under replacements with N = 2n_0 + k.
- Cut movement for opposite-root commutators (Lemma 5.1 via the commutator identity), including the counting of allowed cut positions against rules of length at most k.
- The wrong-row subgroup U(S,P): all commutator cases (consecutive, reverse, opposite, diagonal H_i), why it is abelian of exponent 2, and injectivity via the word basis.
- Relocation in three steps: unused columns via the strip, the basis change Q with P = Q^{-1}, and removal of wrong-row factors. Also that rho is a ring homomorphism on F_2 + R_{>=M}.
- The odd-power identity W_z(C_L) = z^L: commutation of factors at different offsets, including the opposite-root case through Lemma 5.2.
- The long-entry representative from the normal closure, using a spare coordinate h.
- The wrap-removal strip enlargement under b > 2(m+1)delta, and faithfulness in triangular evaluation.
- 2-power torsion by conjugating C_{2^a} to unitriangular form.
- Theorem 6.4's order of quantifiers: L is chosen from a fixed representative before the long representative is chosen, which is valid because W_z(C_L) depends only on z.
- Finiteness of the quotients (Schur plus perfectness) and torsion in G.
I compared the quoted hierarchy input with the companion's Prop (finite-rules) item 2 and Theorem thm:algebra; they match (cuts read off single letters, unique token decomposition, [t] = [E(u_t)], L_h = 2*2^h + 1, which is odd).
sibling_notes: The redis hash for family 247 was empty when I checked. This paper's correctness rests entirely on the companion "An infinite finitely presented periodic group" (Sep-23): the matrix-nil theorem thm:algebra, the hierarchy Prop (finite-rules) item 2 with its token/cut decomposition, and the centrality and stability Prop 5.x. Any gap found in the companion's hierarchy or cancellation sections carries over directly to this paper. The extra assumption here, D > 10(c+1)(k+1), is never actually used.
